about.title: Anaheim Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A wet floor with no sign out. A parking lot pothole nobody bothered to fill. A stairwell where the light burned out weeks ago. Falls like these happen quietly across Anaheim, a city of roughly 350,000 people in Orange County, and the person who gets hurt is usually just running an ordinary errand. California premises liability law turns on one question more than any other: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard and fail to fix it or warn you? Lawyers call that notice, and it is what our team will work to establish on your behalf. Evidence fades quickly. Surveillance footage from a store along Ball Road or an apartment complex off Lincoln Avenue can be overwritten within days, which is why reaching out early makes a real difference. You generally have two years to file, and considerably less time when a city or county agency owns the property. Our team works on contingency, so there is no fee unless you recover.

items.question: I tripped on a broken sidewalk in Anaheim. Is that different from falling inside a store?
items.answer: It can be, and the difference matters. When a sidewalk or other property is owned by the City of Anaheim, Orange County, or another government agency, California requires a formal claim within a much shorter window than the two years that applies to private owners. Figuring out who actually owns and maintains the spot where you fell is one of the first things we will sort out, so it helps to reach out soon.

items.question: The store says I wasn't paying attention. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not in California. The state follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by whatever share of blame is assigned to you rather than eliminated. If the owner had notice of the hazard and did nothing about it, that failure still counts against them. We can evaluate how fault might be divided in your situation.

items.question: What should I do right now if I was hurt in a fall on someone else's property?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable, because some fall injuries show up later. Then photograph the hazard, the surrounding area, and your shoes, and write down the names of anyone who saw what happened. Ask the property manager for an incident report and request that any camera footage be kept. We can then review your case at no cost and take it from there.
